findings.summary: The new FE0/LID profile has no composed strict local target handoff and device-lifetime admission contract.
findings.evidence: 90/migration.md:247-273 promises ordinary/snapshot FE0 Attach and usable I/O after normal #79 checks, and binds LID to replica grants/sessions/read handles/cleanup. No #90 appendix defines LID in the local target/device admission path. At the mapped dependency HEADs, #83 fresh-process-contract.md:23-38 requires a current-process FLCH for target startup and explicitly refuses FirstEpoch0 target lifetimes; #15 device-lifetime-contract.md:19-43 requires FIRST_EPOCH to be nonzero in device-info/detach-device and the validated lifetime tuple; #79 initialization-contract.md:133-147 requires that exact tuple and a purpose1 FLCH even for normal noninitializing attach. Thus a proven FE0 volume can pass the newly added replica profile and enrollment verification yet cannot start a strict target or pass CSI device admission when these supported features are composed. The new AttachIdentityVolume contract in90/budgets.md:83-94 also carries neither a process nonce nor returned handoff.
findings.fix: Have #90 specify its whoever-lands-second integration for proven FE0/LID at the strict local target boundary: how fresh-epoch FLCH issuance/verification accepts and binds the signed FLCTv3 identity (including paged Attach), and how #15 device-info/detach lifetime plus #79 normal attach intents persist and compare the exact LID while preserving process nonce/epoch/device checks. Keep dependency plans read-only. Add concrete normal target/CSI and paged-legacy acceptance tests, stale/wrong-LID and handoff refusal, and restart/lost-reply cases; retain the prohibition on fresh-filesystem initialization for legacy data.
